info.name: PizzaHub - Vendor Orders API tests
info.description: See docs/VENDOR_ORDERS_TESTING.md. Run the folders top to bottom, in a fresh Postman session, against a demo database (not your real one).

item.name: 2. Setup (2 vendors, 2 customers, approved items, 5 pending orders)
Set a new runId and delivery days
Vendor One: sign up (ok if the user already exists)

exec: pm.test("signed up, or the user already exists", () => pm.expect([200, 400, 409, 422]).to.include(pm.response.code));
pm.test("token received", () => { const t = pm.response.json().token; pm.expect(t).to.be.a("string"); pm.collectionVariables.set("vendorToken", t); });

request.description: Uses the session cookie stored by the sign-in request right above it.

item.name: Admin approves the item of vendor 1
Admin approves the item of vendor 2

exec: pm.test("4 orders (vendor 2's is not here), newest first", () => { pm.expect(b.data.length).to.equal(4); pm.expect(b.pagination.totalItems).to.equal(4); pm.expect(b.data[0]._id).to.equal(pm.collectionVariables.get("order4Id")); });

pm.test("customer name and item, no email", () => { pm.expect(b.data[0].customer).to.have.property("name"); pm.expect(b.data[0].item).to.have.property("itemName"); pm.expect("email" in b.data[0].customer).to.equal(false); });

pm.test("1 left on page 2", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.data.length).to.equal(1); pm.expect(b.pagination.totalPages).to.equal(2); pm.expect(b.pagination.hasNextPage).to.equal(false); });
